card.title: More Committed Than You
card.instruction: Treat belief in the scene’s strangest premise as a contest, proving your commitment through increasingly unnecessary demonstrations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You only bow to our invisible queen? I'm giving her my chair.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She already has an invisible throne.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then mine can support her feet. You hadn't considered her comfort.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll give her my cushion, then. You can sit down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your cushion. She can have my bed. I'll sleep standing in case she calls.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 outdoes B's bow with a chair, A3 converts the existing throne into a need for A's footrest, and A5 surpasses B's cushion with bed and standing vigilance.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's invisible throne causes A3's foot-support reinterpretation; B4's cushion and seat offer cause A5's larger sacrifice.

relationship.evidence: B2 provides the queen's existing accommodation and B4 offers comfort for both queen and A.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's generous solution as another demonstration to exceed rather than as permission to rest.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a shared invisible-queen belief and explicit comparison of gestures.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's sleep-standing plan follows the bed sacrifice and B4's sit-down offer.
